assets.source_citation: ISO 19906 / IACS Polar Class global ice pressure decreasing with contact area: p_G = p_ref*(h/h_ref)^-0.5 with p_ref = 1.2 MPa at h_ref = 1.0 m, as implemented in TensorPhysics hullgirder/ice_load.py::global_ice_pressure

tolerance.note: rule-form pressure used as an order-of-magnitude global level

assets.verification_note: Anchored to the ISO 19906 / Polar Class global-pressure level as transcribed in this repository (p_ref = 1.2 MPa at 1 m); the standard clause was not read during this build, so both the 1.2 MPa level and the -0.5 thickness exponent are repo-transcribed values with rule-level (not experimental) authority.

assets.source_citation: Riska/Kujala pressure-area family p = p0*A^-0.45 (ISO 19906 Annex A form) with reference pressure p0 = 3.0 MPa at A = 1 m^2 for first-year ice

tolerance.note: covers the p0 reference-pressure band (2.4-3.6 MPa) and the exponent band

assets.verification_note: Power law is the cited rule form; the reference pressure p0 = 3.0 MPa is the nominal first-year local pressure used in this repository (ice_plasticity/iso19906.py::typical_ice_belt_params), i.e. a nominal engineering value with a 2.4-3.6 MPa band, not a measured datum.

assets.source_citation: ISO 19906 (2010) Annex A pressure-area relation p = p0*A^-ex with ex = 0.45 for first-year ice, as used by the Riska/Kujala pressure-area family and transcribed in TensorPhysics ice_plasticity/iso19906.py

tolerance.note: exponent band quoted for first-year ice local pressure

assets.verification_note: Exponent 0.45 is the value used in this repository and in the ISO 19906-derived pressure-area practice; the ISO document itself is paywalled and was not opened, so the band 0.40-0.55 is the literature scatter, not a verbatim table.
